name: Callaway Quantum Max
community_verdict: Longest fairway wood tested in 2026 — the only model to surpass 260 yards of carry in independent testing. Speed Wave 2.0 with 40g floating tungsten and Step Sole design for clean turf interaction. AI-optimised face retains 94% ball speed on mishits. Sam Burns and Jon Rahm both adopted it quickly on tour. The benchmark all-round fairway wood for 2026.

name: Callaway Quantum Max D
community_verdict: Callaway's easiest fairway wood to hit with high launch, maximum forgiveness, and slight draw bias. Larger footprint and shallower face promote easy launch and natural square delivery. Speed Wave 2.0 frees up face flex especially on low-face strikes — the most common miss with fairway woods. Best for high handicappers who struggle to get the ball airborne from the deck.

name: Callaway Elyte Fairway
community_verdict: Previous gen now heavily discounted — one of the best performing fairway woods of 2025 now available at $299. Confident all-rounder with Tungsten Speed Wave and Step Sole. Long from tee and turf. Gamed by Xander Schauffele and Jon Rahm on tour. Exceptional value at this price for mid handicappers.

name: Callaway Quantum Hybrid
community_verdict: Callaway's 2026 flagship hybrid with Optifit 4 hosel offering seven loft and lie combinations including ±2 degree lie adjustment — particularly useful given the common left miss with hybrids. AI Smart Flex face optimises speed, spin, launch and accuracy across the full face. Consistent ball flight from any lie. Five lofts from 22-34 degrees to replace any long iron.

name: Callaway Elyte Hybrid
community_verdict: Previous gen hybrid now on sale at a significant discount. Testers praised the launch monitor data — a well rounded versatile hybrid that excelled from a range of different lies. One of the best performing hybrids of 2025 now available at under $250. Hard to beat at this price for mid-high handicappers.

name: TaylorMade Qi4D Fairway
community_verdict: Built on the Qi35 which completed the grand slam at the 2025 majors — all four winners used TaylorMade fairway woods. Refined for 2026 with TAS adjustable weights and improved Speed Pocket. Twist Face technology corrects toe and heel mishits. Five lofts including a 9-wood for golfers who prefer more height and soft landing. Rory McIlroy in the bag.

name: TaylorMade Qi4D Tour Fairway
community_verdict: Tour-spec fairway wood with three-position TAS weighting for precise CG control and shot shape. More compact profile than the standard Qi4D for better players who want workability. Lower spin and more penetrating flight than the Max models. Used by tour professionals across the TaylorMade roster. Not for high handicappers — demands consistent ball striking.

name: TaylorMade Qi4D Max Fairway
community_verdict: Maximum forgiveness fairway wood from TaylorMade with enlarged footprint and V-Steel sole for easy glide through the turf. Single 8g rear TAS weight pushes CG deep for high launch and improved carry up to 220+ yards on 3-wood strikes. Twist Face straightens toe and heel contacts. Best for high handicappers who struggle with fairway woods from the deck.

name: TaylorMade Qi4D Rescue
community_verdict: TaylorMade's 2026 flagship hybrid with 8g TAS weight and 3-degree loft sleeve. Progressive top line — slightly thinner than Max models — for a more confident look for better players. Multi-material 450 stainless steel and carbon fiber crown. Designed to hit specific carry yardages with steep descent angle to hold greens. Three lofts cover 2-4 hybrid range.

name: TaylorMade Qi4D Max Rescue
community_verdict: Maximum forgiveness hybrid for high handicappers and slower swingers who want long iron replacements that actually get the ball up. Five lofts from 20-34 degrees replace everything from a 3 hybrid to a 7 hybrid. Thicker top line provides confidence at address. Ideal for golfers transitioning away from long irons who need maximum help launching hybrids.

name: TaylorMade Qi35 Fairway
community_verdict: The fairway wood that completed the 2025 major grand slam. All four major winners used TaylorMade fairway woods. Now discounted as previous gen — one of the best performing fairway woods of 2025 available at a fraction of the original price. Twist Face, Speed Pocket, Infinity Carbon Crown. The Qi4D is a refinement not a revolution — the Qi35 is still outstanding.

name: Titleist GT2 Fairway
community_verdict: High launch, low spin, and forgiving — an unusual combination that makes the GT2 a perfect fairway wood alternative from the tee. Tour players requested higher launch with the same spin rates from the TSR2 and Titleist delivered. Proprietary Matrix Polymer crown is 5x lighter than steel, lowering CG for that high flight. Forged L-Cup face retains speed on low strikes. Now discounted from $399.

name: Titleist GT3 Fairway
community_verdict: Tour-level fairway wood with deeper face and compact profile for better players who hit down on the ball. CG Track adjustability for dialling in flight and workability. Low spin with penetrating flight. Now discounted from $399 — outstanding value for a tour-spec fairway wood. Multiple PGA Tour wins in the GT3. Not suitable for high handicappers who need help launching.

name: Titleist GT2 Hybrid
community_verdict: 10% higher MOI than the TSR2 hybrid. Sleeker profile with flush leading edge for better turf interaction. Heel-toe CG adjustability for fade bias and precise alignment. Forged L-Cup face for speed on low strikes. The most versatile hybrid in the GT family — comfortable off the tee, from the rough, and as a long approach club. Most popular hybrid on the Titleist tour staff.

name: Titleist GT1 Hybrid
community_verdict: Titleist's most forgiving hybrid — 5% higher MOI than the TSR1. Longer face heel to toe for more real estate and better ball speed on off-centre strikes. Forward-aft adjustable weights to control launch. Fairway wood shaft insertion standard — softer and higher balance point suits slower swing speeds. Best for high handicappers replacing long irons who need maximum help.

name: Ping G440 Max Fairway
community_verdict: Five lofts including a new 4-wood for precise gapping. Carbonfly Wrap crown lowers CG for high-launching performance off the ground. Free Hosel technology creates a 4% taller face for confidence off the tee without raising CG height. Face thickness optimised at heel and toe for consistent performance across the face. Ping's most versatile fairway wood for the widest range of golfers.

name: Ping G440 LST Fairway
community_verdict: Low spin multi-material fairway wood for faster swingers who want a penetrating flight. Viktor Hovland carries the LST on tour. High launch with low spin — the hardest combination to achieve in fairway wood design. Less forgiving than the Max but rewards consistent ball strikers with extra distance and a controlled flight window. 3 and 5 wood only.

name: Ping G440 SFT Fairway
community_verdict: Draw-biased fairway wood with straight flight technology that corrects slices from the fairway and tee. Same SFT technology as the driver — heel-biased CG turns pushes and fades into playable draws. Not for straight hitters or hookers. If you slice your driver and carry a matching SFT fairway wood the consistency of correction on both clubs is extremely satisfying.

name: Ping G440 Hybrid
community_verdict: Six lofts from 17-34 degrees — the widest range of any hybrid in the category. Carbonfly Wrap crown and Spinsistency grooves for consistent spin rates across the full face. Free Hosel technology reduces hosel mass for better CG positioning. Matches perfectly with the G440 fairway and driver for a cohesive set. Viktor Hovland in the bag.

name: Mizuno ST-X 230 Fairway
community_verdict: Mizuno's all-round fairway wood now at a significant discount. Forged SAT2041 Beta Ti face for fast ball speeds. Draw-biased heel weighting for a natural right-to-left flight. Loved by Mizuno loyalists for feel and sound quality that rivals much more expensive fairway woods. Now at just $249 — one of the best value fairway woods available anywhere.

name: Mizuno JPX One Fairway
community_verdict: Mizuno's 2026 flagship fairway wood matching the JPX One driver. Superb aesthetics with premium feel at address. Slightly higher spin than competitors but delivers impressive consistency and accuracy. Reviewers note it looks and sounds outstanding — classic Mizuno quality. Best for Mizuno loyalists who want a matching fairway and driver from the same family.

name: Mizuno CLK Hybrid
community_verdict: Outstanding value Mizuno hybrid that delivers the brand's signature feel at a very accessible price. Wave sole technology for fast ball speeds. Four lofts from 18-27 degrees. Previous gen but still competitive with anything on the market. Under $200 makes it one of the best value hybrids available — Mizuno quality for mid-range money.

name: Cobra OPTM X Fairway
community_verdict: All-round fairway wood from Cobra's 2026 OPTM family. H.O.T. Face technology expands the sweet spot for consistent speed. PWR-Bridge suspended weight design. FutureFit33 hosel for 33 loft and lie combinations. Bridges the gap between elite performance and everyday playability. The OPTM X is a gem that successfully suits most golfer types at mid handicap.

name: Cobra DS-Adapt X Fairway
community_verdict: Previous gen now significantly discounted. Strong performer in 2025 testing with impressive distance numbers. Two adjustable weights for spin settings. Now at $249 — outstanding value for a well-rounded fairway wood that suits a wide range of mid handicappers. The OPTM X is better but at $100 less the DS-Adapt X is extremely compelling.

name: Cobra King Hybrid
community_verdict: Cobra's 2026 hybrid with MIM precision construction for tighter tolerances. Flight Window Technology optimises CG per loft for optimal trajectory at each yardage. Matches the King irons and wedges for a cohesive Cobra setup. Four lofts from 17-26 degrees. Good mid-handicap option for golfers who want modern performance at a competitive price.

name: Srixon ZXi Fairway
community_verdict: Best low spin fairway wood of 2025 according to Golf Monthly. ZXi maintains Srixon's reputation for low-spin performance that helps faster swingers keep their flight under control. Laser face milling for precise spin rates. Matching the ZXi iron family creates a cohesive setup. Shane Lowry played these at the TGL debut. Excellent value versus Titleist and TaylorMade.

name: Srixon ZXi Hybrid
community_verdict: Srixon's 2025 flagship hybrid with i-Flex face structure and laser face milling for consistent spin and speed. Premium forged feel that punches above its weight against Titleist and TaylorMade at a lower price. Matches the ZXi iron and fairway wood family. Tour validated by Brooks Koepka and Hideki Matsuyama. Four lofts from 17-26 degrees.

name: Wilson DYNAPWR Carbon Fairway
community_verdict: Award-winning fairway wood that rivals clubs costing twice as much. Full carbon crown construction saves weight for lower CG and better sound. PKR-360 AI face delivers impressive distance and forgiveness. Reviewers compare it to a Titleist GT3 in looks and performance at a fraction of the price. If you're not brand-led this is one of the best fairway woods available at any price.

name: Wilson DYNAPWR Hybrid
community_verdict: Wilson's game improvement hybrid with PKR-360 AI face and carbon crown construction. High launch for easy long iron replacement. Significantly cheaper than equivalent Ping, Titleist and TaylorMade hybrids with comparable performance. Matches the DYNAPWR driver and fairway wood family. Excellent value option for golfers transitioning away from long irons on a budget.
